title: Right knee osteoarthritis with three-view X-ray
encounterNote: 62-year-old male presents with six months of right knee pain that worsens with stairs and walking. He denies locking, instability, or recent trauma. Examination: right knee crepitus, mild effusion, and no ligamentous instability. A three-view X-ray of the right knee shows joint space narrowing and osteophytes. Assessment: primary osteoarthritis of the right knee. He was advised on physical therapy and topical NSAIDs.
